children: Hometown Financial Group, a New England community bank holding company, filed an S-1 to convert from a mutual holding company to a fully public stock company. The company plans to list on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the ticker “HFG.” It aims to raise roughly $510 million to $690 million (up to $793.5 million) at $10.00 per share to fund organic growth, repay debt, and support its pending acquisition of Primary Bank.

Hometown Financial Group is a bank holding company for TruNorth Bank, a Massachusetts-chartered savings bank with 55 branches across Massachusetts, northeastern Connecticut, and southern New Hampshire. The bank gathers deposits and lends primarily in one- to four-family residential mortgages, commercial real estate, multifamily, construction, home equity, and commercial business loans. It also provides wealth management services and operates a mortgage banking division (TruNorth Mortgage) that originates loans for sale and for its portfolio.

Following years of growth through mergers, the company recently unified brands under TruNorth Bank and intends to focus more on organic growth. It plans to use IPO proceeds to strengthen capital and liquidity, repay senior debt, support the pending acquisition of Primary Bank in New Hampshire, expand commercial lending capabilities, invest in technology and infrastructure, and consider targeted expansion opportunities. Management emphasizes disciplined underwriting, a strong risk governance framework, and a diversified funding strategy, including initiatives to grow core deposits.
: Operates across Massachusetts, northeastern Connecticut, and southern New Hampshire; Boston-Cambridge-Newton MSA population ~5.1 million with median household income of $121,960.
: Boston MSA population projected to grow ~2.14% from 2026–2031; Massachusetts projected to grow ~1.78% over the same period.
: 55 banking offices; ranked 12th in Massachusetts by deposits, 16th in New Hampshire, and 38th in Connecticut.
: Large money-center and regional banks, community banks, credit unions, fintechs, and non-bank lenders.
: Ongoing consolidation, focus on core deposits and liquidity, expansion of digital channels, prudent credit risk management.
: 55 banking offices across MA, CT (northeastern), and NH (southern); 8 additional operations/loan offices
: Essex, Hampshire, Hampden, Middlesex, Norfolk, Plymouth, Worcester (MA); Northeastern CT; Rockingham County (NH), with planned expansion via Primary Bank
: IntraFi reciprocal deposits for expanded FDIC coverage; LPL Financial for wealth management
: Total assets $6.94B; Deposits $5.81B; Loans $5.46B; Core deposits 63.3% of total deposits; Municipal deposits $772.3M; Employees 706 FTE
: 37.3% one- to four‑family residential; 34.3% commercial real estate; 11.4% multifamily; 4.5% construction; 5.3% home equity; 7.2% commercial business
: Non-performing assets 1.19% of total assets; non-accrual loans 1.42% of total loans
: Total interest and dividend income of $349.3 million and non‑interest income of $32.0 million (FY2026)
: Interest and dividend income grew 12.2% year-over-year (from $311.3 million to $349.3 million)
, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer - Career community banker; CEO since 2013; previously CEO of bankHometown and former FDIC examiner.
, President and Director - Former CEO/President roles at North Shore Bank and Beverly Bank; extensive leadership across Massachusetts community banks.
, Chief Financial Officer, Treasurer and Assistant Secretary - Joined in 2025; previously Treasurer at Brookline Bancorp; earlier roles at State Street, FHLB Boston, and a banking advisory firm.
, EVP, Chief Risk Officer - Nearly 40 years of banking experience; former CEO of two independent Midwest banks; joined via North Shore Bank acquisition.
, EVP, Chief Retail and Marketing Officer - Leads retail and marketing; prior executive roles at United Financial/United Bank; active in regional philanthropy.

: Contribute at least 50% to TruNorth Bank; fund ~$85.4 million cash portion of Primary Bank acquisition; repay $135 million senior note due 2027; loan ~$49.9 million to ESOP; retain remainder for investments and general corporate purposes.
